Colore: Siena & pale grey Collezione: Sectile 1729 Codice: 5800 Materiale: 100% Cotton Disegno: Damask Scala: Medium Altezza: 140 cm Rapporto: 32.5 cm × 69 cm Toni: Yellow MARMORINO takes its name from the traditional Venetian plaster finish — a surface that mimics the qualities of stone through layered application rather than actual marble. Colore: Verde antico & pale grey Collezione: Sectile 1729 Codice: 5805 Materiale: 100% Cotton Disegno: Damask Scala: Large Altezza: 140 cm Rapporto: 130 cm × 141 cm Toni: Green NAVATA takes its six-medallion pattern from the marble ornament of I Gesuiti, the church of Santa Maria Assunta in Venice (built 1715–1729), whose white-and-green Baroque stonework is one of the most ingenious feats of decorative craftsmanship in the city's history. Between 1725 and 1731, the church's walls, floors, and pillars were sheathed in inlaid white-and-green marble worked to imitate the damask and silk wall-hangings then in vogue in Venice — stone made to pass for fabric. The conceit reaches its height in the pulpit carved by Francesco Bonazza, where marble falls in soft drapery as though a curtain had been hung and then turned to stone, a material paradox that sits at the heart of what SECTILE 1729 does as a collection . NAVATA translates that logic into a large-scale printed cotton: a pattern that carries architectural scale and Baroque ornamental richness. It is a Venetian fabric in the most literal sense — produced in Venice, from Venice, about Venice. Produced in collaboration with Venetian Heritage.

Colore: Sage & gold Collezione: Lucis Codice: FF-8001 Materiale: 100% Cotton Disegno: Damask Scala: Large Altezza: 141 cm Rapporto: 47 cm × 74.5 cm Toni: Yellow, Green LUCREZIA is one of Fortuny's most classic patterns printed on velvet — a 17th-century Italian design that pays tribute to ‘Lucretia,’ the ancient Roman noblewoman immortalized by Rembrandt in 1664. In large plumes and intricate tendrils, the motifs unfold across a densely decorated field: symmetrical, balanced, and rich with the formal authority of baroque decorative tradition. The large-scale repeat makes LUCREZIA a natural choice for expansive wall applications and generous drapery where the full composition can be read. On upholstery, the scale commands attention — although it is suited well to both statement pieces and s upporting roles. Finished with Fortuny's metallic pigments on a cashmere-cotton ground, LUCREZIA brings quiet luxury and timeless decorative presence to refined interiors.

Colore: Whippet & silvery gold Collezione: The Philosopher's Stone Codice: FF-8011 Materiale: 100% Cotton Disegno: Tribal Scala: Small Altezza: 140 cm Rapporto: 19.5 cm × 17.5 cm Toni: Light grey MORESCO is one of Fortuny's foundational patterns, introduced in the early 1900s as one of the first designs Mariano Fortuny printed, and still among the most popular in the catalog. Its dense motif of geometric and organic forms draws from the Moorish heritage of his birthplace, Granada , Spain: a city whose Alhambra palace represents the apex of Medieval Iberian and North African ornamental culture, best expressed in the mosaic tilework and arabesque structure of its walls and ceilings. MORESCO translates that visual intelligence into a large-scale printed surface that reads as architecturally complete at any scale. Part of THE PHILOSOPHER'S STONE collection , available in the jewel-tone palette that defines the collection.
